hypothesis: STIFF (motion-pathway) type-to-type connections are more consistent across two independent specimens than SLOPPY (photoreceptor / lamina wide-field) connections.

specimens.A: FlyWire FAFB v783, adult female, right optic lobe (Dorkenwald et al. 2024; typing Matsliah et al. 2024)
specimens.B: Janelia Male CNS v0.9, adult male, right optic lobe (Berg et al. 2025; = optic-lobe v1.0 volume of Nern et al. 2025)

mapping_decisions: Generic 'T4' represented by listed subtypes T4a/T4c/T4d; T4b excluded (not listed stiff).
R1..R6 pooled to 'R1-6' (both datasets annotate outer PRs as one pooled type; individual identities untestable).
maleCNS R7p/R7y/R7d pooled to R7; R8p/R8y/R8d pooled to R8 (Sup.Table7 3-to-1 match).
Right optic lobe only, both specimens. maleCNS side=somaSide else rootSide.
maleCNS: all typed bodies included regardless of proofreading status.

Counts summed over all neuron instances per type and all neuropils; FlyWire connections table is thresholded at >=5 synapses/neuron-pair by the Codex release; the same >=5 per-neuron-pair threshold was applied to the maleCNS weights table for comparability.
